docs.title: GitHub API Documentation (Basic Guide)
docs.text:
Welcome to this beginner-friendly documentation for the GitHub REST API.

This guide is created by a technical writer who is not a developer – and that's the point! If you're curious about APIs but don't know where to start, you're in the right place.

docs.title: What is an API?
docs.text: An API (Application Programming Interface) allows different programs to talk to each other. In this case, GitHub provides a set of URLs you can send requests to in order to get information about repositories, issues, users, and more.

docs.title: What does it mean to 'interact with the GitHub API using HTTP requests'?
docs.text:
It means you can use tools like your browser, terminal, or Postman to send messages to GitHub and get responses. These messages follow a specific format using URLs and often include tokens (like passwords) to authenticate.

Example request: 

GET https://api.github.com/users/octocat

This would return data about the user "octocat".

docs.title: Why this guide?
docs.text: This documentation was written with clarity and simplicity in mind. It's for anyone who wants to understand the basics of APIs without being overwhelmed by code.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: To interact with the GitHub API, you need to authenticate using a personal access token.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "login": "octocat",
  "id": 1,
  "name": "The Octocat"
}

👉 Replace YOUR-TOKEN with your actual GitHub token.

docs.title: Issues
docs.text: Create, list, or update issues for a repository.

docs.title: Example Request Body
docs.text:
{
  "title": "Bug: Unexpected logout",
  "body": "I was logged out after 5 minutes of inactivity.",
  "labels": ["bug"]
}

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text: Work with public or private repositories using these endpoints.
